name: Combobox
description: An input widget with an associated popup (listbox, grid, tree, or dialog) that helps users set a value by selecting from a collection of possible values, supporting editable and select-only variants.

keyboard_interactions.action: Opens popup if closed; moves focus to first item or item after auto-selected suggestion
(Optional) Opens popup and places focus on the last item
Dismisses the popup if visible; optionally clears the value
Accepts the current autocomplete suggestion or selected value
(Optional) Displays the popup without moving focus into it
(Optional) Closes the popup or returns focus to combobox

roles.description: Identifies the element as a combobox

required_attributes.description: Goes on the INPUT element (ARIA 1.2). The old ARIA 1.0 pattern put it on a wrapper div — that is obsolete and breaks in current screen readers.
References the popup's id. The popup must stay in the DOM for this to resolve.
State. On the input, not the wrapper. false when the popup is hidden.

optional_attributes.description: Set to 'grid', 'tree', or 'dialog' if popup is not a listbox
The id of the visually-active option, while DOM focus STAYS on the input. This is the core of the pattern: never call .focus() on an option as well — pick one mechanism.
true on the active option only. Since it is not real focus, this attribute is also what your CSS must key off to show the highlight.

notes: The combobox is one of the most complex ARIA patterns — test thoroughly with screen readers

For a select-only combobox, use native <select>. It is keyboard-complete, screen-reader-complete, and works on mobile. Only build the ARIA pattern when you genuinely need filtering, multi-select chips, or rich option markup.
role='combobox' goes on the <input>, per ARIA 1.2. The ARIA 1.0 pattern (role='combobox' on a wrapper div with the input inside) is obsolete — do not copy old tutorials.
aria-activedescendant means DOM focus never leaves the input. Options must not be tabbable and must never be .focus()ed.
Because the active option has no real focus, the browser will NOT scroll it into view. You must call scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' }) yourself.
Announce the result count through a separate polite live region (RAWeb 7.5). Never put aria-live on the listbox itself — it will read every option on every keystroke.
Clear aria-activedescendant when the popup closes, or the input keeps announcing an option that is no longer visible.
<datalist> looks like the native answer but its screen reader support and styling are too limited to depend on.
native_element: <select> for select-only (strongly preferred). No native element for autocomplete — <datalist> support is too poor to rely on.

raweb_criteria.reason: combobox/listbox/option roles, aria-expanded and the active option must all be exposed — nothing here is conveyed by a native element.
Arrows must open and traverse the list, Escape must close, Enter must select — all without a pointer.
Filtering is a status message: '3 results available' must be announced via a live region, or a screen reader user types and hears nothing back.
The active option's highlight is NOT real focus, so :focus-visible never fires on it. You must style [aria-selected=true] yourself or the keyboard user sees nothing move.
The combobox is a form input field and needs a real associated label.
Tab must always close the popup and leave the widget.
